title: Canonical compactification comparison on bounded-below etale origin
statement: Let $\Lambda$ be a finite commutative ring, $f:X\to Y$ a quasi-compact morphism of schemes, and $c,d$ two compactifications of $f$ [def-weil-compactifications-refinements]. Use the derived categories of fixed $\Lambda$-module sheaves on the small etale and pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories] and [def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules]. Let $D^+_{et}(X_{proet},\Lambda)$ be the full subcategory of bounded-below etale-origin objects, namely the objects isomorphic to $\nu_X^*L$ for some $L\in D^+(X_{et},\Lambda)$ [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism]. The compact-support candidates are the restrictions of $Rf_!^c=Rp_*j_!$ and $Rf_!^d$ [def-compact-support-direct-image-detailed]. Define their canonical natural comparison $I_{c,d}:Rf_!^c\xrightarrow{\sim}Rf_!^d$ on this full subcategory by transporting the ordinary etale comparison through the canonical compact-support site comparisons and the equivalence $\nu_X^*:D^+(X_{et},\Lambda)\simeq D^+_{et}(X_{proet},\Lambda)$. The etale comparison is the comparison from $c$ to their common refinement $c\wedge d$ followed by the inverse comparison from $d$ to that common refinement. This fixes the comparison, rather than supplying an arbitrary isomorphism.
